notes.claim: A poor power factor can be corrected by adding a load drawing equal and opposite reactive power, which means a capacitor for an inductive load.
Correction does not change the true power consumed, but cuts apparent power and the total current drawn from the source.
Too much capacitance gives a low power factor just as too much inductance does, so a correction must not over-correct.

sources.title: Lessons In Electric Circuits -- Volume II (AC) - Chapter 11
sources.quote: Poor power factor can be corrected, paradoxically, by adding another load to the circuit drawing an equal and opposite amount of reactive power

sources.title: Lessons In Electric Circuits -- Volume II (AC) - Chapter 11
sources.quote: This correction, of course, will not change the amount of true power consumed by the load, but it will result in a substantial reduction of apparent power, and of the total current drawn from the 240 Volt source

sources.title: Lessons In Electric Circuits -- Volume II (AC) - Chapter 11
sources.quote: It should be noted that too much capacitance in an AC circuit will result in a low power factor just as well as too much inductance. You must be careful not to over-correct when adding capacitance to an AC circuit.
